why: The Washington County moratorium (ORD-2026-12) pauses all data center applications countywide through June 2027, but the evidence does not explicitly confirm that the ordinance extends into the incorporated city of Hagerstown; if it does apply, the project cannot obtain local permits until the moratorium lifts. The site’s prior permitting status is also unknown, so the grandfathering exemption for existing Certificates of Use & Occupancy cannot be ruled out. Separately, the project’s 121 diesel generators (302.5 MW) trigger a federal Title V major-source permit due to an estimated 1,067 tpy of NOx, which adds a substantial air-permitting burden. These combined jurisdictional and permitting uncertainties require confirmation before a definitive go/no-go decision.

needs_confirmation.text: The why-chain assumes that if the county moratorium applies to Hagerstown city, it would block the project's local permits. However, the evidence does not establish that Washington County has permitting authority over data center projects within the incorporated city of Hagerstown. In Maryland, incorporated municipalities typically have their own zoning and permitting authority. The moratorium's scope "within Washington County" may refer only to unincorporated areas. The draft's link between the moratorium and the inability to obtain local permits is unverified.
